newsitem.title: UK: Odds on Clarke becoming Conservative leader cut.
newsitem.headline: Odds on Clarke becoming Conservative leader cut.

text.p: The odds on British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke becoming the next leader of the ruling Conservative party have been slashed to 3-1 from 10-1, Ladbrokes bookmakers said on Thursday.

Clarke has been under attack from right-wing Conservatives this week for his strong support for a single currency. Ladbrokes said this led to "significant" betting interest in Clarke taking over from John Major as party leader if the Conservatives lose the next election.
He is now joint favourite with Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell at 3-1.
Home Secretary Michael Howard is 4-1, Defence Secretary Michael Portillo 5-1 and ex-cabinet minister John Redwood 6-1.
Labour remains 2-5 to win an election due by next May. The Conservatives are quoted at 7-4 and the Liberal Democrats 250-1, William Hill bookmakers said.
Labour was 2-9 at the beginning of the year and a William Hill spokesman said there were now indications the odds gap between the two main parties may begin to grow again.
Much may depend on what happens at party conferences over the next two weeks, he said.
